findings.where: Nav bar, the logo lockup at top left (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The logo is shown all in white: white thin arches and a white serif 'MMM INFRA'. The logo's blue #0070C0 and grey #404040 are gone, the arches look thinner than the mark's heavy tapered band, and 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' is left out. The diazo-blue ground leaves no place where the real logo could sit at 3:1, so the whole direction depends on a white version that the client does not hold.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo the brief says 'stays' and is 'never redrawn'. The house's never-recolour rule also says a white version is made only with the client's yes. A returning client would not recognise the house blue.

findings.where: Hero, the line under the name ('…with over 40 years of international infrastructure experience')
findings.fault: The one line of proof on the first screen leans on a size word ('over 40 years'). It names no body, role, region or date that a reader could check. It is also written in the third person ('from a former Lead Lawyer'), not in Mark's own voice.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff who hire against terms of reference. They judge by checkable specifics, not by counts of years. Mark asked to be the person heard in his own words, not described like a firm.

findings.where: Whole page: no footer and no email address on the page; the only contact is the 'WRITE TO MARK' mailto button
findings.fault: Mark's email address is never shown as text. A visitor whose mail client does not open from a mailto link has no address to copy. The page ends on the motion sketch frame with no contact route.
findings.who_objects: Agency staff on locked-down work machines, where mailto often does nothing. They need an address they can paste into their own mail.

findings.where: Whole page, and above all the article specimen ('AN ARTICLE PAGE'): long light text set on saturated diazo blue over the full grid
findings.fault: On the article page the ground meant for the opening picture becomes the reading surface. The grid lines run under every line of prose, and paragraphs are reversed out in light type on mid-blue. A full-length article or a PDF gateway page would be tiring to read and noisy. The tile does not show a calmer ground for Read mode.
findings.who_objects: Readers of Mark's articles, who read long legal and policy arguments. Angélique too, because every post she adds lands on this busy ground.

findings.where: Whole tile: no place for a photograph of Mark
findings.fault: The look shows no photograph and no way one would sit on the blueprint sheet. There is no frame, no treatment and no ground for it. The man himself is never seen.
findings.who_objects: First-time visitors, who look for a real face before writing to a solo advisor. Mark and the brief, whose value 3 is 'Mark is seen and heard'; Mark also asked for images from his LinkedIn posts.

findings.where: Nav bar, the title-block cells 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001' and 'SCALE NTS' (top right on desktop, top row on phone)
findings.fault: Two static cells sit in the same ruled row as the four nav links, boxed the same way and in the same light colour, so they look like more nav items. Their content is a made-up drawing number and 'not to scale', which means nothing to a visitor. On phone they take the top row and push the real navigation down a row.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page and gets nothing. Mark too, who finds busy headers off-putting.

findings.where: Hero name block: the circled 'A' section marker and the subtitle 'LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS' under 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR'
findings.fault: Drawing jargon sits in the name block and gets the same type and weight as his role. This dilutes the one line that says who he is, and it reads as costume.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor scanning for what Mark does, who has to read past 'longitudinal section' to find out. Mark, who asked for nothing busy.

findings.where: Hero drawing (the amber hatch in the third arch) and the palette's 'SODIUM AMBER: daylight in the drawing, and the one action'
findings.fault: The primary action's amber also colours a piece of decoration in the drawing, so one colour has two jobs. It is the second most eye-catching patch on the first screen and weakens the button's claim to be the one amber thing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor squinting for the next step, whose eye goes to the hatched arch before the button.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the loose S-curve rising at the right of the ground line (desktop; trailing at right on phone)
findings.fault: A stray curve with no label rises off the ground line beside the arches. It belongs to no part of the section drawing and reads as a drawing error.
findings.who_objects: Engineers and infrastructure staff, who read drawings and would see a line with no meaning.

findings.where: Type pair rule ('Headings in ExtraBold capitals, tracked wide') against the article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The tile states one heading treatment and its own article specimen breaks it, setting the title in title case without tracking. The layout round gets two conflicting answers for headings.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer and Angélique, who need one rule for a new post's title.

findings.where: Dates and separators: article meta '18 September 2024' (sans, long form) against the lecture row '2026-04-23' (mono, ISO); '•' and '·' mixed in 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF', and '•' in the hero against '·' in 'CUT · MEASURED · EXACT'
findings.fault: Dates in the same specimen use two faces and two formats, and two different dot separators sit side by side.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader, who sees the inconsistency. Angélique, who needs one pattern to copy.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'REPLAY THE CUT' button
findings.fault: It is a button but looks like a link, with underlined spaced capitals, the same mark as the article's link.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined label to take them somewhere and instead sees the drawing animate.

findings.fault: The earth-hatch box runs into the frame's left edge, and the poche box runs to the right edge with no matching inset. Below them an empty band with a rule makes the specimen look broken at phone width.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reviewing the tile on a phone, Mark included, who sees a sloppy frame on a direction meant to read as exact.

findings.fault: The Element column is squeezed to a few words per line ('The poche / wipes along the / cut, left to right / (clip-path)'), and the Easing column says only 'plot', which tells no reader what it means.
findings.who_objects: The animation round's designer, who has to read the table for timing and easing.
